newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian government fights to ride out new scandal.
newsitem.headline: Belgian government fights to ride out new scandal.

text.p: Belgium's centre-left government fought for its life on Tuesday as pressure mounted on the scandal-hit Francophone Socialist Party (PS) to leave the coalition and police raided the party's Brussels headquarters.

Social Affairs Minister Magda de Galan said her party had "received the message loud and clear" from Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene that the PS should clean up its act and make clear who was to blame in a new bribery scandal.
"We know what we have to do," she said, without elaborating.
She also dismissed calls by a liberal opposition leader for the government to resign.
The PS is the second most powerful partner in Belgium's four-party coalition government with the Flemish Socialists and the French- and Flemish-speaking Christian Democratic parties.

The latest scandal erupted when Merry Hermanus and Francois Pirot, two former top PS officials, were arrested last week as part of a probe into allegations that the party received kickbacks from French aviation firm Dassault.
Dassault has denied any wrongdoing.
The two men were charged on Monday with corruption. They are alleged to have taken 30 million Belgian francs (about $1 million) from Dassault in 1989 as a contribution to party funds.
Hermanus says Guy Spitaels, then PS president and currently president of the Walloon Regional Parliament, knew of the contribution according to Hermanus's lawyer.

Spitaels, forced to resign in 1994 during investigations into bribes allegedly paid to the PS in the late 1980s by Italian helicopter firm Agusta in exchange for a lucrative army contract, denies all knowledge of the Dassault money.
Spitaels was re-elected in 1995.

The Agusta investigations also brought down NATO Secretary General and Flemish Socialist Party member Willy Claes 18 months ago. Claes, who was Economy Minister at the end of the 1980s, also maintains his innocence.
Claude Eerdekens, head of the PS parliamentary party, told RTBF television there was a possibility the chamber might be forced to lift Spitaels's ministerial immunity from prosecution.
Philippe Busquin, current president of the PS and also implicated in the Dassault affair by Hermanus, also denied any knowledge of the latest allegations.

But on Tuesday morning, acting on instructions from the Liege public prosecutor and the Cour de Cassation, Belgium's highest court, plain-clothes police searched the accounts department of the PS headquarters, removing several files.
The scandal is the latest in a string of set-backs for the government and the PS in particular.

In December, after weeks of turmoil, the government used its parliamentary muscle to throw out a string of allegations that Deputy Prime Minister and PS member Elio Di Rupo had sex with boys under the legal age of consent of 16 years.
Di Rupo had always rejected the allegations but the parliamentary move nevetherless prompted cries of cover-up.
National elections are not due until 1999, but if the PS does succumb to the pressure and quit the coalition the government will fall.

However Dehaene, with his eyes firmly set on Belgium joining the European Union's single currency at the start of 1999 is anxious to avoid either changing partners in mid-stream or calling early elections.
